stage_description: The senior stage begins in the last quarter of expected lifespan and depends heavily on size: small breeds from 11+ years, medium from 9+, large from 7+, and giant breeds from 5–6 years. Age-related changes appear: lower activity, possible joint, vision, and hearing problems, and cognitive decline. The goal of care is early disease detection and maintaining comfort and quality of life.
nutrition: A senior formula with digestible protein (given healthy kidney function) and calorie control. Joint supplements may be indicated; any dietary change should be discussed with the veterinarian, especially where chronic disease is present.
activity: Gentle, regular walks and swimming to maintain muscle and joint mobility; avoid jumping and sudden exertion. Mental enrichment helps slow cognitive aging and keeps the dog engaged.
veterinary_check_frequency: Exams every 6 months with blood chemistry, urinalysis, and blood-pressure monitoring to catch age-related disease early.
dental_care: Regular dental assessment — periodontal disease is particularly common at this stage and can affect the heart and kidneys. Professional cleaning is done as indicated, weighing anesthetic risk.
warning_signs: Disorientation, tremors, changes in toileting habits, hearing or vision loss, noticeable weight loss, signs of pain, and limping. Any of these warrants a veterinary evaluation.
disclaimer: This information is for educational purposes only and does not replace consultation with a veterinarian.
